parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the Clipper test20 task, exact CLI/output requirements, no-crates constraint, black-box binary inference rule, and root /output/test20.rs delivery requirement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept local ownership of oracle construction and Rust writing while launching a workflow to have children derive Clipper2 layout and decompilation facts.
parallel.implementation: The parent built a gdb oracle/tracer, wrote formatter, core, pipeline, engine, offset, and root test20.rs files, and relied partly on child layout reports for Clipper internals.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact contained root test20.rs plus src/clipper modules, so packaging met the entry-file requirement even though the implementation failed all official tests.
parallel.verification: The parent ran reference samples, oracle traces, formatter tests, geometry comparisons, and local differential checks, but did not complete the planned workflow merge/decompile/verify phases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The offset/constants layout child was killed before returning; the final implementation was incomplete or incorrect enough that official evaluation passed zero of forty cases.

serial.requirements: The serial run worked from the same prompt and recognized the need for a pure Rust 2021 implementation with no dependencies and exact reference behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent locally owned exploration, oracle construction, engine implementation, validation, and edits with workflows and delegation disabled.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote Cargo.toml plus src/core.rs, src/stdsort.rs, and src/engine.rs, building a substantial local Clipper engine from disassembly and oracle probes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Despite local module work, artifact validation found only Cargo.toml and src files and did not find the required root test20.rs entry file.
serial.verification: The serial run ran reference outputs, gdb probes, an intersection check, a stage validator, and fixed a preserve_collinear default before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial solution still timed out and failed delivery validation because the required root entry artifact was missing; current official evaluation also passed zero of forty cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had the same prompt and recognized root test20.rs, exact output, pure Rust 2021, no external dependencies, and black-box inference obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same prompt and requirements, including the root entry file and exact CLI/output behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference is evidenced; the later difference is delivery and coordination execution, not task understanding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work between a parent local implementation path and a workflow whose first phase delegated three layout tasks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation, probing, and verification work in the main agent with workflow and task tools disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child lifecycle and join dependencies; serial had a single-owner local path and therefore no child lifecycle exposure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed and componentized around Clipper internals, with merge depending on all three layout reports being available.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained the prompt, probe results, disassembly findings, and implementation state inside one local trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an explicit handoff interface between layout reports and downstream merge/decompile stages; serial did not need cross-agent handoff contracts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built oracle infrastructure and wrote multiple /output/src/clipper modules plus root test20.rs while waiting for layout findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a Cargo project and wrote core/stdsort/engine modules, then iterated on validation locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered a root entry file and a broader module tree, while serial produced source modules but omitted the required root entry file from the artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow returned two layout results but the offset/constants branch stalled, retried, and remained in progress when the workflow was killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; its lifecycle was a single local stream ending by timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Only parallel had an adverse child-result lifecycle; serial's closure problem was not child-result timing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel artifact validation copied a directory containing root test20.rs and six src/clipper module files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation copied Cargo.toml and three src files, but expected_entry test20.rs was absent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel met final artifact placement; serial failed required root entry placement even though both implementations failed the official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran reference outputs, gdb/oracle checks, formatter tests, geometry checks, and then official evaluation passed zero cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran reference outputs, gdb probes, an intersection check, a stage validator, and then official evaluation passed zero cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both performed substantial local checks that were not sufficient for official acceptance; the official outcome is equal at 0/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed essentially the whole 2400 second budget and exited 143 with the workflow killed before all child results were complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also consumed essentially the whole budget and exited 143, but with workflows disabled and no child state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out; only parallel's closure included a killed active workflow branch, while serial's closure included a missing root deliverable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status.json evaluations give both modes solution_passed=false and 0/40, so there is no discordant official outcome. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel delivered the required root test20.rs artifact but its workflow was killed before completing the offset/constants layout dependency and the implementation still failed all tests; serial pursued the work locally without delegation but omitted the required root test20.rs artifact and also failed all tests.
parallel_contributors: Parallel produced a root artifact and several source modules, but the implementation remained incorrect enough for 0/40.
The parallel workflow lost the offset/constants branch before downstream merge/decompile/verify phases could consume a complete layout set.
serial_contributors: Serial produced local Cargo and source modules but artifact validation did not find expected_entry test20.rs.
Serial had no child lifecycle issue and no delegation, but still timed out and failed official tests.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's implemented module tree and root file differ from serial's Cargo/src-only artifact.
Serial's root-artifact omission is a delivery defect rather than a parallel coordination pattern.
evaluator_effects: Serial cell/evaluation/summary.json is stale and incomplete after a retry; the completed retry in cell/status.json is authoritative.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences are comparative context, not an explanation for a discordant result

candidates.reason: The parent actively owned and wrote the implementation while children owned research/layout slices; implementation was not ownerless.
The parent retained integration responsibility and wrote the final module tree; the adverse episode is an unfinished child, not unowned integration.
Parallel artifact validation shows a root test20.rs and module files, so final assembly ownership was present even though behavior failed.
The workflow and parent defined an end-to-end research-to-implementation pipeline; it was interrupted rather than left without an owner.
Implementation and oracle work proceeded in parallel with the workflow; productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight.
The parent did not defer all implementation until after investigation; it wrote and tested Rust modules while workflow children investigated layouts.
The same chain is better represented by explicit early termination of the active offset/constants child; starvation is not separately evidenced.
There were three layout children and retries, but the retained direct boundary is a killed active child, not collective breadth alone exhausting budget.
The offset/constants brief was large, but the directly observed failure is cancellation before a needed result, not proven overbroad scope as the primary boundary.
The layout child briefs included task, binary, tool, precision, and deliverable requirements; no already-known required fact is shown missing from a child brief.
The workflow specified report paths and merge inputs for the separately owned layout reports; no incompatible independently produced components are evidenced.
No known finding is shown disappearing during transfer; two completed layout summaries are present and the missing offset result never transferred.
Returned layout summaries were large but were not shown to be available and unconsumed because of volume; the chain was blocked by a missing child result.
No parent action is shown consuming a superseded child report or obsolete workspace state; the workflow did not reach the dependent merge result.
No incompatible child reports are shown reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated; the third layout report was absent.
Parallel did not present a completed workflow-derived solution based on a partial workflow result; official failure alone cannot establish this label.
The retry lacked a final returned result, but there is insufficient evidence that it repeated prior work because a checkpoint was omitted rather than continuing the same scope.

candidates.reason: The workflow executed child agents, required the offset/constants layout result for merge, and was killed while that retry child was still active, preventing a needed result from finalizing.
candidates.realized_consequence: The planned workflow stopped before the offset/constants layout result finalized, so the merge, decompile, and verifier phases depending on all three layout reports never produced an aggregate result for the parent.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is downstream of the same cancellation chain; the directly evidenced boundary is explicit termination of an active child before its needed result finalized.

No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the workflow never reached the verifier phase.
The same workflow chain is already captured as early termination; there is no separate child failure return followed by an independent refusal to take over.
Completed core and auxiliary layout results were recorded in the workflow journal; no available completed result is shown ignored by the parent.
Although the workflow stalled and retried, the more direct and sufficient boundary is the killed active child before final result, not blind waiting over available progress.
No competing concurrently written implementation designs are shown requiring reconciliation across different files.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file with one observing or reconciling the other change.
No non-entry source file produced or owned by one concurrent actor is shown deleted, replaced, or wholesale rewritten by another.
No required entry file or submitted artifact is shown overwritten while another agent owned or used that deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion is shown replacing multiple final outputs and invalidating another agent's work.
Agents used shared notes, but no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem from unisolated shared writes is evidenced.
No generated artifact, cache, temporary file, or auxiliary implementation from one actor is shown contaminating another actor's verification or implementation.
